text: Warfarin acts as a potent inhibitor of the enzyme vitamin K epoxide reductase complex subunit 1 (VKORC1). By blocking this enzyme, warfarin prevents the recycling of vitamin K, thereby inhibiting the gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (II, VII, IX, and X) and reducing the risk of thromboembolism. This interaction is well-documented and serves as the primary pharmacological mechanism for warfarin's anticoagulant effect.
